nodes.name: NTIA and federal users (DoD, FAA, NOAA)
nodes.description: Federal agencies hold much of 1-10 GHz. The 2025 budget law requires 500 MHz of federal spectrum in 1.3-10.5 GHz to be repurposed (200 MHz identified by July 2027 for auction by July 2029); 2.7 GHz relocation plans were approved in April 2026 and the 7.125-7.4 GHz study is due December 2026. The FirstNet Authority (Band 14) also sits in this group.
nodes.size_label: 800 MHz statutory pipeline, 500 MHz of it federal

nodes.name: FCC auction program
nodes.description: Auction authority restored to Sept 30, 2034. Lower C-band (Auction 107) raised $81.17B in 2021; the AWS-3 re-auction (Auction 113) raised $3.57B in June 2026, 88% from Verizon; upper C-band (Auction 115, 160 MHz) starts April 27, 2027 with a TD Cowen estimate of $30-75B.

nodes.name: Satellite (MSS) band licences and ITU coordination
nodes.description: Big LEO, L-band and 2 GHz mobile-satellite bands are assigned administratively with ITU filings, not auctioned. In April 2026 the FCC kept incumbents exclusive (DA 26-398); WRC-27 item 1.13 studies satellite use of IMT bands from 694 MHz to 2.7 GHz, and an Oct 2026 FCC proposal would add 482 MHz to satellite-terrestrial sharing (SCS).
nodes.size_label: MSS bands: 2 GHz (40 MHz), Big LEO (~25 MHz), L-band (~40+ MHz)

nodes.name: SES (incl. Intelsat), C-band satellite incumbents
nodes.description: Satellite operators cleared 3.7-4.0 GHz for the 2021 C-band auction and received about $9.7B of accelerated relocation payments (SES ~$4.0B, Intelsat ~$4.9B; prior knowledge), and SES completed its purchase of Intelsat in 2025 (prior knowledge). They are also the incumbents in upper C-band, where clearing is estimated at $4.33B plus about $6.3B of incentive payments for Auction 115.

nodes.name: Ericsson
nodes.description: Largest US radio-network (RAN) supplier; Dell'Oro puts Ericsson above 60% of North American RAN in 1H 2025. Holds AT&T's ~$14B five-year Open RAN contract (Dec 2023, prior knowledge) plus large Verizon and T-Mobile shares.
nodes.size_label: Est. US RAN and private-5G sales ~$4.4-6.3B/yr

nodes.name: Nokia
nodes.description: Second US RAN vendor, mainly T-Mobile, after AT&T moved to Ericsson; also sells private wireless to utilities and industry. Its Nov 2026 traffic report projects AI driving 44% of network traffic by 2035.
nodes.size_label: Est. US RAN and private wireless ~$1.0-1.9B/yr

nodes.name: Samsung Networks
nodes.description: Virtualized RAN supplier to Verizon (five-year ~$6.6B deal from 2020, prior knowledge), including C-band, and a supplier of CBRS radios to cable operators.

nodes.name: Qualcomm
nodes.description: Main supplier of 5G modems and Snapdragon chips for US Android phones, FWA gateways and connected cars, and still in most iPhones. It is losing iPhone modem share to Apple's in-house C1 chips.

nodes.name: MediaTek
nodes.description: Supplies chips for mid- and low-end Android phones, FWA customer equipment and cellular IoT modules sold in the US.

nodes.name: Apple modems (C1/C1X)
nodes.description: Apple's in-house cellular modems, first shipped in 2025 iPhones, replace Qualcomm parts over time. This is an internal transfer inside Apple, shown at an estimated equivalent value.
nodes.size_label: Est. ~$0.5-1.2B/yr of US iPhone modem content

nodes.name: Satellite builders (MDA, Thales Alenia, Airbus, Swissto12)
nodes.description: Builders of mobile-satellite and direct-to-device spacecraft and payloads. SpaceX and AST SpaceMobile build their own satellites; MDA builds Apple-funded replacements for Globalstar.
nodes.size_label: Est. D2D/MSS satellite orders ~$0.4-1.0B/yr (excl. SpaceX in-house)

nodes.name: American Tower
nodes.description: Largest US tower REIT. Total 2025 property revenue was $10.3B; it guides US and Canada organic tenant billings growth of ~0.5% for 2026 (~4.5% excluding DISH churn), with DISH in default.

nodes.name: Crown Castle
nodes.description: Tower-only since the sale of its fiber and small-cell units closed May 1, 2026. 2026 site rental revenue outlook is $3.85-3.90B; Bloomberg reported SpaceX talks over site access.

nodes.name: SBA Communications
nodes.description: Third national tower REIT. Domestic site leasing was ~$1.87B in 2025 (sum of quarters); its 2026 outlook removes all EchoStar contracted revenue.

nodes.name: Small cells and DAS (Zayo/EQT, ExteNet, Boldyn)
nodes.description: Street-level small cells and indoor distributed antenna systems that densify the grid. WIA counted 198,100 outdoor small cells and 830,350 indoor nodes at end-2025; Crown Castle's small-cell unit went to Zayo/EQT in 2026.

nodes.name: Fiber backhaul (Lumen, Zayo, cable, others)
nodes.description: Fiber links from cell sites to the core. T-Mobile buys most of its backhaul; AT&T and Verizon largely use their own fiber.

nodes.name: Launch providers (SpaceX Falcon 9, Blue Origin, ISRO, Firefly)
nodes.description: SpaceX launches its own Direct to Cell fleet in-house (internal, not shown as a flow). AST has more than 100 BlueBirds under launch contracts for 2027-28 and a $1.3B Firefly engine deal for its own Blacklift rocket; the May 2026 New Glenn failure is a schedule risk.
nodes.size_label: Est. D2D/MSS launch spend ~$0.35-0.85B/yr (excl. SpaceX in-house)

nodes.name: AT&T
nodes.description: Holds ~314-375 MHz sub-6 GHz after closing EchoStar's 30 MHz of 3.45 GHz and 20 MHz of 600 MHz for $22.65B on July 28, 2026; runs FirstNet. Q3 2026 wireless service revenue $17.76B (+5.0%); licences on the books at $149.4B.
nodes.size_label: Wireless service revenue ~$70B/yr (2026 run-rate); ~314-375 MHz sub-6 GHz

nodes.name: Verizon
nodes.description: Holds ~279-290 MHz sub-6 GHz and ~1,700 MHz of mmWave; won ~$3.16B of the 2026 AWS-3 re-auction and bought Array's 850 MHz/AWS/PCS for $1.0B. Hosts the cable MVNOs; Q3 2026 postpaid ARPA fell 1.9% while phone adds hit 406k.
nodes.size_label: Wireless service revenue ~$78B/yr (est.); ~279-290 MHz sub-6 GHz

nodes.name: T-Mobile US
nodes.description: Largest sub-6 GHz holder (~376 MHz, 2.5 GHz core). Sold its 800 MHz to Grain for $3.6B (keeps 50% of later gains) and shares its PCS G block with SpaceX for T-Satellite. FY2026 service revenue outlook ~$76.8B; 8.45M FWA customers at end-2025.
nodes.size_label: Service revenue ~$76.8B (FY2026 outlook); ~376 MHz sub-6 GHz

nodes.name: SpaceX (Starlink)
nodes.description: Buying ~79 MHz of terrestrial-usable spectrum: AWS-4/H-block (~$17B) and unpaired AWS-3 (~$2.6B) from EchoStar, in trust until a closing targeted for Nov 30, 2027, and 800 MHz from Grain (~$8B reported, pending FCC). Its ~650 Gen-1 Direct to Cell satellites run on T-Mobile's PCS G block, with FCC approval for 15,000 next-gen; ~22M Starlink Mobile monthly users (Q3 2026); reportedly seeking ~80,000 US cell sites.
nodes.size_label: ~79 MHz owned or pending (0 closed); Q3 2026 revenue ~$14.6B

nodes.name: AST SpaceMobile
nodes.description: 12 BlueBirds operating (Nov 2026), ~45 targeted by mid-2027. Rights to up to 45 MHz of Ligado L-band ($550M plus at least $80M/yr) and 60 MHz of S-band priority ($64.5M); partners AT&T and Verizon. Q3 2026 revenue $42.3M, FY2026 guide $150-200M, cash $3.2B.
nodes.size_label: Up to 45 MHz L-band + 60 MHz S-band rights; FY2026 revenue guide $150-200M

nodes.name: Globalstar (to Amazon)
nodes.description: ~25 MHz of Big LEO mobile-satellite spectrum plus Band 53 terrestrial rights; Apple owns 20% and takes 85% of capacity. Amazon's ~$11.57B purchase (about 40x 2026 sales) was cleared by the FCC on Oct 27, 2026 and should close in 2027.

nodes.name: Iridium (to Rocket Lab)
nodes.description: Global L-band satellite operator (~9-10 MHz, unverified) with 2025 revenue of $871.7M. NTN Direct goes commercial for Deutsche Telekom IoT in Q4 2026; Rocket Lab is buying it at $54/share (EV ~$8.0B), closing mid-2027.

nodes.name: Viasat (Inmarsat)
nodes.description: Holds global L-band satellite rights through Inmarsat and EU 2 GHz rights that expire in May 2027. It disputes AST/Ligado L-band rights outside North America and supplies L-band capacity behind Skylo-based phone satellite messaging.
nodes.size_label: Global L-band MSS; 2x15 MHz EU 2 GHz (unverified)

nodes.name: Ligado Networks
nodes.description: L-band holder in its second bankruptcy (2025). It leased up to 40-45 MHz to AST for $550M, mostly passed to Inmarsat, plus at least $80M/yr, against ~$8.6B of funded debt (weak source).
nodes.size_label: ~40 MHz L-band (North America); ~$8.6B debt at Chapter 11

nodes.name: Comcast (Xfinity Mobile)
nodes.description: About 10.6M mobile lines (+368k in Q3 2026) as a Verizon MVNO with CBRS offload; about half of Q3 connects were free lines. Holds 600 MHz (paid ~$1.7B; leased to T-Mobile and being sold for up to $3.3B, mostly ~2028) and CBRS licences.

nodes.name: Charter (incl. Cox)
nodes.description: Spectrum Mobile has 13.5M lines including Cox (+508k pro forma in Q3 2026), mainly as a Verizon MVNO with CBRS offload. Holds 210 CBRS PALs bought for $464M; T-Mobile hosts its business lines.

nodes.name: EchoStar (remaining licences)
nodes.description: Sold 3.45 GHz/600 MHz to AT&T ($22.65B, closed) and AWS-4/H-block/unpaired AWS-3 to SpaceX (~$19.6B, in trust, closing ~Nov 2027). It keeps paired AWS-3 remnants, 700 MHz E block, CBRS and mmWave (book $8.45B), to be sold by Sept 2028; Boost now runs as a hybrid MVNO on AT&T.
nodes.size_label: Remaining licences book $8.45B (Sep 30, 2026); 261.8M SpaceX shares due

nodes.name: Grain Management
nodes.description: Private spectrum investor. Bought T-Mobile's nationwide 800 MHz for $3.6B (closed Aug 10, 2026) and agreed on Oct 8 to resell it to SpaceX for a reported ~$8B, pending FCC approval.
nodes.size_label: Up to 14 MHz of 800 MHz (546 licences), sale pending

nodes.name: Array Digital Infrastructure (ex-UScellular)
nodes.description: Former UScellular. Sold its operations and ~30% of its spectrum to T-Mobile ($4.4B incl. debt) and licences to AT&T ($1.018B) and Verizon ($1.0B); keeps its C-band, mmWave and towers.

nodes.name: Anterix
nodes.description: Nationwide 900 MHz broadband licences sold or leased to utilities for private LTE. After the FCC widened the band from 6 to 10 MHz in Feb 2026, it put its spectrum value at $2.5B to over $7B.
nodes.size_label: 900 MHz (3x3 MHz, widening to 5x5); own value est. $2.5-7B+

nodes.name: NextNav
nodes.description: Holds ~8 MHz of lower 900 MHz location licences and petitions the FCC to reconfigure 15 MHz for 5G positioning and broadband. A draft rule went to White House review in March 2026 and faces heavy opposition.

nodes.name: CBRS users, utilities and enterprises
nodes.description: CBRS offers 150 MHz shared with Navy radar (70 MHz licensed PALs, the rest free GAA access); about 228 PAL winners include utilities, WISPs and enterprises, and utilities also run private LTE on Anterix 900 MHz. SNS expects private 5G spending of $6.6B a year globally by 2030.
nodes.size_label: CBRS 150 MHz (70 MHz PAL); PALs sold for $4.59B (2020)

nodes.name: Postpaid retail plans
nodes.description: Big 3 consumer and small-business postpaid plans. In Q3 2026 Verizon added 406k phones while ARPA fell 1.9%, AT&T added 379k, and T-Mobile raised ARPA 4%.

nodes.name: Prepaid brands (Metro, Cricket, Total/Visible, Boost)
nodes.description: Carrier-owned prepaid and digital brands plus Boost. Verizon core prepaid ARPU was $33.51 in Q3 2026 (+2.5%).

nodes.name: MVNO and wholesale (cable on Verizon, Boost on AT&T)
nodes.description: Resold network capacity: ~24M cable lines on Verizon, Boost as a hybrid MVNO on AT&T, and smaller MVNOs on T-Mobile. Inflows overlap, because cable retail revenue includes the wholesale it pays Verizon.
nodes.size_label: ~24M cable lines plus Boost and other MVNOs

nodes.name: Fixed wireless access
nodes.description: Home and business broadband over licensed mid-band, about 19M Big 3 lines by Q3 2026 (Whitesail est.). A line uses ~500 GB/month against ~25 GB for a phone; New Street expects industry adds to slow to 3.6M in 2026.

nodes.name: IoT and connected-car wholesale
nodes.description: Bulk data plans for car makers, telematics, meters and trackers, plus satellite IoT. Ericsson counts 4.5B cellular IoT connections worldwide (2025); connected-car traffic stays under 1% of mobile traffic through 2029.

nodes.name: Satellite add-on plans (T-Satellite, Skylo, AST beta)
nodes.description: Satellite texting and light data in coverage gaps. T-Mobile's Starlink-based T-Satellite (since July 2025) was 0.0002% of T-Mobile network usage; Verizon and Google phones use Skylo; AST runs a beta with AT&T and Verizon.

nodes.name: Enterprise and government contracts (incl. FirstNet)
nodes.description: Large enterprise and public-sector wireless contracts, including AT&T's FirstNet public-safety network. FirstNet's authority expires Feb 22, 2027 unless reauthorized; its 4.9 GHz band-manager order was upheld in July 2026.

nodes.name: Private LTE/5G network services
nodes.description: Private networks for factories, ports, utilities and campuses, built on CBRS, 900 MHz or carrier spectrum by carriers, vendors and integrators.

nodes.name: Consumers (households)
nodes.description: US households on about 603M connections; service revenue per connection was $33.14/month (CTIA). 82-89% of smartphone data goes over Wi-Fi (Opensignal, 2024).
nodes.size_label: US wireless service revenue ~$235B (2025, all customers)

nodes.name: Businesses and enterprises
nodes.description: Companies buying phone lines, IoT/telematics, FWA and private networks; robot makers recommend private 5G for industrial sites.

nodes.name: Government and public safety (FirstNet)
nodes.description: Federal, state and local agencies and first responders; FirstNet runs on AT&T with Band 14, and satellite operators sell L-band and Starlink services to the US government.
nodes.size_label: Est. ~$5.5-9B/yr of wireless and satellite spend

nodes.name: Auto makers and robotaxi fleets
nodes.description: Car makers buy modems and bulk data for embedded connectivity; Waymo ran about 4,000 robotaxis in Sept 2026, each producing ~20 GB/day (AT&T estimate).

nodes.name: Device makers (Apple, Samsung, Google, Meta)
nodes.description: Handset, wearable and glasses makers buy modems and satellite capacity. Apple owns 20% of Globalstar and takes 85% of its capacity; Meta and EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7M smart glasses in 2025.

nodes.name: Smartphones
nodes.description: About 326M US phones averaging ~25 GB/month of cellular data (Ericsson North America, 2025), forecast at 52 GB by 2031.
nodes.size_label: ~98 EB/yr of ~159 EB US traffic (2025, Whitesail est.)

nodes.name: Home broadband via FWA
nodes.description: Fixed wireless homes and offices are the largest new load on licensed mid-band; Bubley estimated FWA made up ~90% of the 2023 US traffic increase.

nodes.name: Connected cars and robotaxis
nodes.description: Embedded car connectivity and robotaxis. Waymo's ~4,000 vehicles equal ~0.02% of 2025 US traffic; even 1M robotaxis would add ~4.6%.

nodes.name: Wearables and AI glasses
nodes.description: Cellular smartwatches and AI glasses, which mostly connect through the phone. IDC sees display-less glasses at 13.6M units in 2026 and 27.3M by 2030 (global).

nodes.name: IoT and robots
nodes.description: Sensors, trackers, delivery robots and industrial robots; Counterpoint expects >50,000 humanoid shipments in 2026, mostly indoors on Wi-Fi or private 5G.

nodes.name: Drones
nodes.description: Cellular-connected drones for inspection, delivery and first response; with robotaxis, one of the outdoor moving uses where licensed wide-area spectrum matters most.

nodes.name: Rural and off-grid coverage
nodes.description: Coverage-gap texting and data via direct-to-device satellites, plus Starlink broadband in rural areas. Satellites reach roughly rural, not urban, capacity per km2.
nodes.size_label: D2D revenue well under $1B/yr globally (2026, Whitesail est.)

network.notes:
Map built 2026-11-20 from the research digest (brief.md) and workflow_result.json, plus 5 of the 8 allowed web searches: AMT 2025 results, Crown Castle 2026 outlook, Dell'Oro RAN share, SBA 2025 domestic leasing, and cable mobile revenue (the last found nothing usable). The map has 54 nodes and 128 edges: 37 spectrum and 91 flow. SpaceX (Starlink) is the only focus node.

How to read values. Flow edges are yearly money, at 2025 or 2026 run-rates, in USD millions. Spectrum edges are one-off deal or auction values on the date shown, so their widths should not be compared with yearly flows. Pending deals are labelled pending: EchoStar to SpaceX (in trust, closing ~Nov 2027), Grain to SpaceX (~$8B is WSJ-reported, not disclosed), Comcast 600 MHz to T-Mobile, Ligado to AST, and Amazon-Globalstar and Rocket Lab-Iridium, which are folded into their nodes.

Where values are firm. These come from FCC results or filings: the Auction 107 and 113 winner amounts, the 600 MHz auction amounts, EchoStar-AT&T $22.65B, the EchoStar-SpaceX ~$17B and ~$2.6B, T-Mobile-Grain $3.6B, the Array sales, Ligado-AST $550M plus at least $80M a year, and the Anterix 2026 sales.

Where values are recalled, not re-verified. AT&T ~$9.1B in Auction 110, UScellular ~$1.28B in C-band, Cox CBRS ~$213M, DISH ~$13.3B gross in Auction 97, AT&T's ~$18B of FirstNet fees, the AT&T-Ericsson ~$14B and Verizon-Samsung ~$6.6B contracts, the Verizon $100M commitment to AST, the Iridium EMSS contract, and NextNav revenue.

Whitesail estimates (estimated "Yes"):
- C-band clearing payments are ~$14B allocated pro rata to bid shares.
- Tower lease edges split reported totals (AMT US&C ~$5.2B, CCI ~$3.9B, SBA ~$1.87B) by assumed tenant shares.
- RAN edges assume ~$7-8B a year of US RAN spend, with Ericsson above 60%.
- Carrier-to-channel splits start from reported service revenue: AT&T ~$70B a year from Q3 2026 $17.76B, T-Mobile ~$76.8B FY2026 outlook, and Verizon ~$78B (estimated). Channel shares are assumed, and FWA uses subscriber counts times ~$45-55 a month.
- Satellite D2D flows are small and highly uncertain. SpaceX does not disclose D2D revenue; T-Satellite was 0.0002% of T-Mobile usage.
- The T-Mobile-to-SpaceX PCS G-block edge has no disclosed fee. Its value is the estimated yearly T-Satellite revenue pool.

Known overlaps and exclusions:
- MVNO channel inflows double count, because cable retail revenue includes the wholesale paid to Verizon. The MVNO-to-consumers edge is set net of this.
- Device-maker outflows (phone hardware ~$75-95B) are hardware value added, not spectrum money.
- SpaceX-to-consumers (Starlink broadband, ~$4-6.5B) uses Ku/Ka-band, not mobile spectrum. It is shown for scale on the focus node.
- SpaceX's in-house satellite building and launch are internal and not shown as flows.
- Old auctions (AWS-3 2015 for AT&T and Verizon, Verizon's CBRS PALs) and tower lease flows to Charter and Crown Castle's DISH leases are omitted to stay under 130 edges.
- Globalstar's Big LEO licences were assigned administratively, so they have no spectrum edge.
